summary: Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Lviv and habilitation at Jagiellonian University. He held posts at Lviv, Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń (1945–1953), and the University of Warsaw (1953–1971).

Eugène Burnouf was a French scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian-Central Asian studies who studied under Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He served as secretary of the Société Asiatique and held a teaching post at the Collège de France from 1832 to 1852.

Eugène Denis worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning his PhD from the University of Paris. He was a research scholar at the National Centre for Scientific Research (1961–1986) and held posts at Bangkok University and Chulalongkorn University.

Eugène Henri Guillaume Edgard Monseur was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who earned his doctorate from the University of Liège under Charles Michel. He served as professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Grammar at Université libre de Bruxelles (1888–1912).

Eugène Jacquet was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and sinology who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand. His teachers included Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat, Eugène Burnouf, Antoine-Léonard Chézy, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and Pierre-Amédée Jaubert.

Eugène Obermiller was an expert in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Theodore Stcherbatsky. He served at the Institute of Buddhist Culture, the Institute of Oriental Studies, and the Academy of Sciences of the USSR.

Eugène Pittard was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at the University of Geneva around 1894 to 1899. He later held an academic post at the University of Geneva from around 1916 to 1949.

Eugène Tisserant was a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at the Lycee Notre-Dame Saint-Sigisbert, the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales, and the École du Louvre.

Eugène-Armand Hauvette-Besnault was an Indologist who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He served as librarian at the École Normale Supérieure, taught Sanskrit at the Sorbonne in 1868, and was Directeur des études adjoint pour Sanscrit at the EPHE (circa 1869–1890).
Eugénie Bazin-Foucher was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She completed her studies at the Sorbonne and at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1915–1918) under Sylvain Lévi.

Eugénie Sellers was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Girton College, Cambridge, and the British School at Athens. She held posts at Chatsworth House (1904–1908) and the British School at Rome (1909–1925).

Eun Hino is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed master's studies and served as a project researcher at the University of Tokyo. She later served as an assistant professor and associate professor at Musashino University.
Keiun Maeda was a scholar in Buddhist studies who taught Kozui Otani. During his career, he served as president of Toyo University and president of Ryukoku University.

Eun-su Cho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. She was an assistant professor at the University of Michigan and became professor at Seoul National University in 2004.
Eunyoung Choe is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a doctorate at Korea University. She held a post as an HK professor at Geumgang University, attested between 2013 and 2015.

Eustaquio Echauri Martínez was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Conciliar Seminary of Pamplona and Universidad Central. He served as professor at the University of Barcelona (1920) and Complutense University of Madrid (1940).
Eva De Clercq is an Indologist who earned her PhD at Ghent University between 1999 and 2003. She has held posts there, including as a permanent member in 2025.

Eva K. Neumaier is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She held positions as Professor Emeritus, Chair, and Professor at the University of Alberta and as Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Calgary, both attested in 2006.
Eva K. Neumaier-Dargyay is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Rigzin. She held a post at the University of Calgary, attested in 1992.

Eva Tichy is a linguist and Indologist who earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg and completed her habilitation at the University of Marburg. She held the chair for Indo-European studies at the University of Freiburg (1993–2017).
